title: Decentralized pin schedule and safety grid (scratchpad)
body:
Notes to self — high-level intent:
- Aim: allow many small client-level pins/unpins without central coordination that creates a single blast radius.
- Tradeoffs: slightly slower global stabilization in exchange for minimal synchronized rollback complexity.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- Dedicated routes must maintain latency P95 < 120ms; hosted tier target P95 < 300ms.
- Some tenants (HIPAA customers) must not be exposed to experimental variants — they remain on pinned stable images.
- We have cheap short-lived capacity to warm new variants for 10–20 tenant cohorts concurrently.

Decentralized pin schedule (proposal):
1) Phase 0 — Shadow priming (0% traffic) — 10m per cohort, parallel up to 8 cohorts. Purpose: cold cache fill, observe memory/eviction patterns.
2) Phase 1 — Micro-cohort (0.1% per cohort, 10 tenants) — 15m windows, look for infra regressions (OOMs, GPU saturation).
3) Phase 2 — Gradual take (0.5% -> 2% over 1h) — dynamic if telemetry stable.
4) Phase 3 — Anchoring (5% -> 20% over 6h) — final warmup and priming; allow per-tenant rollback.

Cohort definition heuristics (for pick lists):
- Start: low-LTV, low-concurrency tenants (recent sandbox signups).
- Middle: mid-volume business accounts with strong telemetry history.
- Anchor: high-volume tenants with explicit opt-in SLA for experiment.

Safety grid (signals & thresholds) — quick reference:
- Infra: GPU util > 90% sustained for 2m -> pause new cohort imports.
- Latency: route P95 increase > +35% vs baseline for 5m OR absolute P95 above target -> immediate throttle to previous step.
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.8% absolute OR +200% relative increase (whichever smaller) -> pause and investigate.
- Quality regressions: eval-based scoring on sample prompts drops > 4 points (out of 100) across the cohort -> halt and alert ML lead.
- User complaints: > 3 high-sev CS tickets linked to experiment in 1h -> fast-unpin.

Automated actions (what system should do):
- If infra or latency triggers: reduce new cohort launches and scale up fallback variant (quantized model) for that route.
- If error/quality triggers: immediately roll cohort back to last pinned image, send alert with correlation logs.

Manual checks / checklist before launching a cohort:
- [ ] Confirm image provenance and quantization profile version and checksum.
- [ ] Run smoke script against a synthetic traffic profile for 3 minutes.
- [ ] Confirm warm cache footprint estimate (KV cache estimate < 2x available per worker).
- [ ] Record rollout owner and on-call pager.
- [ ] Post roll note in #releases channel with cohort list and expected timings.

Commands / shorthand (for operator):
- pin(tenant, image) -> pins tenant to image immutably for X hours.
- unpin(tenant) -> revert tenant to route default (honors global rollback policy).
- stage-cohort(image, cohort-id, pct) -> ramp to pct following schedule.
- force-roll(tenant, target-image) -> immediate forced migration (use sparingly).

Telemetry dashboard quick links (placeholders):
- latency rollout dashboard: /dashboards/latency/rollouts
- cohort health: /dashboards/cohort/health
- kv/cache telemetry: /dashboards/cache/evictions

Experiment matrix (examples to try in next week):
- A: small quantized variant (4-bit) vs baseline; hypothesis: cost -20% with <2% quality delta.
- B: batching policy change (max_batch=6 -> 8) for low-latency routes; hypothesis: throughput +15% without P95 regression.
- C: regional warmup (warm in region before global) for multi-region clients; hypothesis: reduces cross-region latency spikes.

Open issues / risk notes:
- Tenant affinity: if we decouple pin schedules too much, dependencies between tenants (shared caches) can create cascading evictions. Need test harness to simulate 40% tenant churn.
- Metric noise: low-volume tenants produce noisy evals; consider aggregate-of-10 policy before making quality decisions.
- Automation race conditions: two operators can pin conflicting images for the same tenant — need last-writer-wins guard plus audit log.

Short-term action items (me):
- [ ] Add a simple simulator that models cache eviction under 30/50/80% churn (due 2025-02-18).
- [ ] Draft a tiny runbook for on-call that describes the five first steps after a P95 spike (due 2025-02-05).
- [ ] Sync with Maya on cohort selection heuristics (PT 30m).

Questions to resolve later:
- Should anchor cohorts be prevented from ever running on quantized variants by policy? Pros: quality stability. Cons: capacity inefficiency.
- How aggressive should automatic unpinning be when multiple low-severity signals are observed concurrently?

Random notes and micro-observations from last dry-run:
- Warmup phase saw a 7% increase in tail latency on worker pool 3 only; correlated with cache eviction storms.
- Client A (low volume) had a transient 1.2% extra 5xx during smoke — looked like a transient OOM on process B.
- Telemetry aggregation window of 1m = too noisy for quality evals; bump sample window to 5m for evaluation triggers.

If anything goes sideways: immediate unpin of impacted tenants, switch client routing to previous stable variant, escalate to ML and infra.

End — this is a scratchpad, messy and iterative. Will refine after simulator results.
